name: Bellhop notifications, HTTP jobs, outbound HTTP and the outbox
description: The notification rules engine on job events, built-in HTTP jobs, the security rules for every outbound HTTP call Bellhop makes, and the EF Core outbox relay for stores without transactional enqueue.

entities.name: NotificationRule
entities.description: A configured rule: trigger, threshold, window, channel, cooldown.

entities.name: Delivery
entities.description: One notification for one rule and subject.

entities.name: HttpCall
entities.description: One outbound HTTP request made by an HTTP job or a webhook channel.

entities.name: OutboxRow
entities.description: A job written to the application's database by the outbox, waiting to be relayed to the job store.

ears.when: a job is dead-lettered
ears.shall: create a delivery for that rule with the job as subject

ears.where: a rule watches repeated failures with threshold N
ears.when: an attempt of a job ends with an exception or a timeout and the job's attempt number is N, whether the job becomes failed or dead-lettered
ears.shall: create a delivery for that rule with the job as subject

requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-5, option 1: failed attempts are counted, including the final one that dead-letters the job. A lease-expiry interruption (jobs REQ-132) is not a failure and does not count. The count is the job's attempt number, so an operator requeue (jobs REQ-141) starts it again.

ears.where: a rule watches the failure rate
ears.when: the failure rate of a job name in the rule's window rises above its threshold
ears.shall: create a delivery for that rule with the job name as subject

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: the rate is always computed per job name, and each job name is its own subject for the cooldown (INV-400).

ears.when: a recurring job's occurrence is missed, starts later than the rule's tolerance after its due time, or has not started when the rule's tolerance after its due time has passed
ears.shall: create a delivery for that rule with the recurring job as subject

requirements.notes: Missed occurrences are read from the record recurring REQ-242 keeps in the store (INV-412), not from REQ-220's in-memory event, so a miss caught by the trigger is alerted even after the next occurrence has finished. refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-6, decided by the owner: notification checks run on nodes with the alerts registration (INV-411), not on workers, so an occurrence that never fired because no worker is alive is still reported, from the stored nextRunAt, by the 'has not started' branch.

ears.when: a node has sent no heartbeat for NodeLostAfter
ears.shall: create a delivery for that rule with the node as subject

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: NodeLostAfter is 5 minutes (hosting REQ-60), longer than the 60 s lease, so jobs of a lost node are recovered well before the alert; fewer false alarms during long pauses and deploys. refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-6, decided by the owner (instead of accepting the gap): the check runs on a node with the alerts registration (INV-411, REQ-438), which can be a worker node, a client or dashboard node, or a node that only does alerts, so the last worker going down is still reported as long as an alerts node runs.

ears.when: a queue's depth rises above the rule's threshold
ears.shall: create a delivery for that rule with the queue as subject

ears.when: jobs have waited on a throttle key for longer than the rule's threshold
ears.shall: create a delivery for that rule with the key as subject

requirements.notes: Reading confirmed by the owner on 2026-11-06: 'throttle key starved' means jobs have waited on the key for longer than the rule's threshold.

ears.shall: never send more than one non-test delivery for the same rule and subject within one subject cooldown; later ones within the subject cooldown are recorded as suppressed

requirements.notes: The source says deliveries are 'rate-limited and deduplicated per rule and subject within a cooldown'. Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: there is also a cap per rule across subjects (INV-407) with a digest at the end of the rule cooldown (REQ-414). refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-1, F-2, F-4: enforced by deciding Pending or Suppressed at creation (INV-409) and keeping a cooldown open while a delivery created in it is still pending (INV-410); the model showed that combination makes INV-400 and INV-407 hold. A failed delivery closes its subject cooldown (REQ-433, F-3).

ears.when: a non-test, non-digest delivery is created for a rule and subject
ears.shall: create it as suppressed if a subject cooldown for that rule and subject is open, or if MaxDeliveriesPerCooldown non-test, non-digest deliveries for the rule were created as pending within its open rule cooldown; otherwise create it as pending and open, for the rule's cooldown length, the subject cooldown and, if none is open, the rule cooldown

requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-1 option 1 (decide at creation, counting deliveries created as pending) and F-4 option 1 (two periods of the rule's cooldown length: one per rule and subject, one per rule). This is the decision rule for the to: [Pending, Suppressed] of REQ-400 to REQ-406. Counting sent deliveries instead fails: two deliveries created before either is sent both see nothing sent. When both the subject cooldown and the cap apply, the delivery counts as deduplicated, not as capped, so it is not in the digest (REQ-414).

ears.while: a non-test, non-digest delivery created within a subject cooldown or a rule cooldown is pending
ears.shall: keep that cooldown open

requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-2 option 1: retries (REQ-412: up to 5 attempts, backoff to 10 min) outlast a typical cooldown, and without this a delivery still retrying is sent alongside the next one. Trade-off accepted: a cooldown can last up to the full retry span, about 20 minutes with the defaults.

ears.when: a non-test, non-digest delivery is marked failed
ears.shall: close the subject cooldown of its rule and subject, so that the next event for that subject creates a pending delivery

requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-3 option 1: deduplication assumes the first delivery reached the channel; a failed first delivery must not silence the rest of the cooldown. The rule cooldown (cap) is not closed. Cost: a channel that stays down produces one Failed delivery per event, each logged by REQ-415.

ears.when: its channel accepts the message
ears.shall: mark the delivery sent

requirements.notes: Channels: generic JSON webhook with a message template, Slack and Teams incoming-webhook presets, ILogger critical, and SMTP email (TECH-115 to TECH-119).

ears.if: its channel rejects the message or cannot be reached, and fewer than NotificationMaxAttempts attempts have been made
ears.shall: retry the delivery with backoff

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: 5 attempts in total with backoff from about 10 s to 10 min, then Failed (REQ-415). Same event as REQ-415 with the complementary guard.

ears.when: an operator presses 'send test' on a rule on the Notifications page
ears.shall: create a test delivery for that rule, outside its cooldown

requirements.notes: Reading confirmed by the owner on 2026-11-06: a test delivery bypasses the cooldown, otherwise a test right after a real alert would be suppressed.

ears.shall: load rules from configuration and from code, use the code definition when a rule with the same name exists in both, and list every rule on the Notifications page

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: code wins, the same precedence as options (hosting REQ-17).

ears.shall: evaluate notification rules, create their deliveries and send deliveries only on a running node that has the alerts registration and holds the notification lease, checking the lease in the same store write that creates or updates the delivery

requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-6, decided by the owner: alerting is its own registration, independent of the client and the worker, so it can run on a worker node, a client or dashboard node, or a node that only does alerts; it keeps working when no worker is alive. The notification check is no longer a worker duty (hosting REQ-40). The lease, fenced in the store write, makes one node the detector, so two nodes noticing the same breach create one delivery (closes modeling assumption A-11). Test deliveries (REQ-409) can be requested from any dashboard node but are sent by the lease holder.

ears.when: no running node with the alerts registration holds an unexpired notification lease
ears.shall: let one running node with the alerts registration take the notification lease for LeaseDuration and renew it every HeartbeatInterval while it runs

requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-6: the same kind of lease as the outbox relay (REQ-435) and the cleanup lease (jobs REQ-164), with the job lease's length and heartbeat (jobs REQ-102) so no new constant is needed.

ears.where: a rule watches an event that is a single recorded state change: a job dead-lettered (REQ-400), an attempt that makes the Nth failure (REQ-401), or a recurring occurrence missed or late (REQ-403); a job that is requeued (jobs REQ-141, REQ-143) can produce such an event again
ears.shall: find those events from what the job store records and mark each one handled for that rule in the same store write that creates its delivery, so that a node that takes over the notification lease neither alerts an event again nor skips one

requirements.rationale: The lease decides which node writes, but these events happen on worker nodes. If the lease holder remembered what it reported in its own memory, a handover would alert an event twice or not at all.
requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 run 2 F-15 (recommended option; the model shows one delivery per event and no event lost with this rule, against a duplicate or a loss with node-local memory). Events that happen while no node holds the lease, or while no alerts node runs at all, are alerted when a holder next runs; the subject cooldown and the cap (INV-409) keep a backlog from flooding the channel. An event is no longer alerted once retention has removed the job it belongs to (jobs REQ-145). State-based rules (REQ-402, REQ-404, REQ-405) need nothing like this: any holder sees the condition, and the subject cooldown handles repeats. How the store records events and the handled mark, for example a per-rule position in a store-assigned sequence of state changes, is an implementation choice. Run 3 F-17 (recommended option): a missed occurrence is found from the record recurring REQ-242 keeps; the last outcome alone is overwritten by the next occurrence, and RunOnce left no trace. Run 3 F-19 (recommended option): each recorded state change is its own event, so a job that is requeued and then dead-lettered again, or reaches attempt N again, is alerted again (REQ-401 notes); a handled mark kept on the job row would hide the second one. Run 3 F-18: where a new rule starts is INV-413.

ears.where: a rule watches an event that is a single recorded state change (INV-412)
ears.when: the notification lease holder evaluates a rule whose name the job store has no record of
ears.shall: record the rule's name in the store and mark every such event the store already records as handled for that rule, without creating deliveries for them

requirements.rationale: Without it, deploying a new rule alerts every once-only event still stored, up to 30 days of dead-letters (jobs REQ-104), or alerts none of them, depending on the implementation.
requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 run 3 F-18 (recommended option): a rule starts at the store's present the first time its name is seen. Its record and handled marks are kept by name even while no node loads the rule, so removing and re-adding it, or a rolling deploy in which the lease moves between nodes with and without it, continues where it stopped and skips nothing. A renamed rule is a new rule.

ears.when: an HTTP job executes
ears.shall: send the request described by its payload through the named HttpClient it references, with the job's request timeout

requirements.notes: HTTP jobs can be enqueued, scheduled or made recurring from code, from the launch page and from configuration.

ears.when: the response arrives
ears.if: its status is one of the accepted status codes and the success predicate, when one is set, holds for the body
ears.shall: mark the job succeeded and store the status, headers and body truncated to the response capture limit as its result

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: the success predicate is a JSONPath with equals or exists (TECH-114).

ears.if: the response status is not accepted, the success predicate does not hold, the request times out, or no response arrives because the connection, name resolution or TLS handshake fails
ears.shall: fail the attempt so the retry policy decides between Failed and DeadLettered, and store the response if there was one

requirements.notes: Reading confirmed by the owner on 2026-11-06: everything that is not an accepted response is an ordinary handler failure, so the retry policy decides between Failed and DeadLettered. With MaxRedirects 0 (REQ-416) a 3xx response is not followed and counts as not accepted unless listed. refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-7 option 1: transport errors are now in the sentence; a destination refused by the security rules is not a failure to retry but REQ-434.

ears.if: its destination is refused by the destination allowlist or the private-address rule
ears.shall: move the job to dead-lettered at once, without sending the request, with a reason that names the rule that refused it

requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-7 option 1: retrying a host that is not allowed cannot succeed, so refusal is permanent. Before this, a refused job stayed Processing for ever because no requirement moved it on and the lease kept being renewed. Run 2 F-14 (recommended option): the redirect rules are no longer listed. INV-403 never follows a redirect to another host, so a followed redirect always lands on the already allowed host, and a redirect that is not followed is a response: accepted if its status is listed (REQ-421), otherwise an ordinary failure (REQ-422), as the owner decided in REQ-422's notes.

ears.shall: never send an HTTP job request or a notification webhook to a host that is not on the configured destination allowlist, which is empty by default

sources.quote: an allowlist of destination hosts (default: none allowed until configured)

ears.if: the destination resolves to a private-network or loopback address and its host name is not itself an entry on the destination allowlist
ears.shall: refuse to send the request

requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-8 option 1: the allowlist entry for the exact host name is the explicit permission; no wildcard entry covers a private address. Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: the check is made on the host name and its resolution before the request, not on the address actually connected to. A name that resolves to a public address at check time and a private one at connect time (DNS rebinding) is therefore not caught; the allowlist (INV-401) is the main defence. Revisit if HTTP jobs ever take destinations from untrusted input.

ears.shall: never follow a redirect to a different host and never follow more than MaxRedirects redirects

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: MaxRedirects is 0 by default (REQ-416), so redirects are not followed unless the application raises it, and then only to the same host.

sources.quote: redirects limited and never across hosts

ears.shall: take Authorization, Proxy-Authorization and Cookie headers and URL user information for outbound calls only from named HttpClient registrations, never from job payloads or configuration templates

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: enforced at creation by INV-408. refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-10 option 1: the sentence now names exactly what is enforced. Other secrets (for example an X-Api-Key header) belong on named HttpClient registrations; the docs say so, but a payload header with another name is not detected.

ears.shall: mask its value in the dashboard and in logs

ears.when: an application calls dbContext.EnqueueAsync
ears.shall: write the job as an outbox row in the application's DbContext so it commits or rolls back with the application's transaction

ears.where: the job store shares the application's database and outbox mode is not configured
ears.when: an application calls dbContext.EnqueueAsync
ears.shall: enqueue directly in the context's current transaction

requirements.notes: The choice between the direct path and the outbox is made by configuration.

ears.when: the relay, running on one worker node that holds the relay lease, processes its next batch
ears.shall: enqueue the row's job in the job store with the row's outboxId as its job id, creating nothing if a job with that id is still stored in any state, and then delete the row

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: the relay deletes relayed rows, so the outbox table stays small. The job store and the application database are different databases in outbox mode, so the two steps cannot share a transaction; idempotency by outboxId (INV-406) covers a crash between them. refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-11 option 1, decided by the owner: the outboxId is the job id and the insert checks every stored job, not only active ones. A unique key would not do, because it is released when the job finishes (jobs REQ-107) and the crash window can end after that. The remaining risk, retention removing the job before a crashed relay is replaced, is covered by assumption REQ-436.

ears.when: no running worker node holds an unexpired relay lease
ears.shall: let one running worker node take the relay lease for LeaseDuration and renew it every HeartbeatInterval while it runs

requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-12 option 1: nothing obliged a node to take over a free relay lease, so a relay crash could leave rows pending for ever. The relay stays a worker duty (hosting REQ-40). Uses the job lease's length and heartbeat (jobs REQ-102) instead of a new RelayLeaseDuration constant.

ears.shall: assume that every finished-job retention (jobs REQ-104) is much longer than LeaseDuration, so a crashed relay is replaced while the job it created is still stored

requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-11: with the defaults (7 to 30 days against 60 s) this holds by a wide margin. If an application sets a retention close to the lease length, a row can be relayed twice. The model cannot judge durations, so this is stated rather than checked. Run 2 F-16 (recommended option, accepted): an operator who deletes an outbox-created job (jobs REQ-144) while the relay that created it has crashed or lost its relay lease and not yet deleted the row gets the job back once. The window is at most LeaseDuration, and the operator gets an extra job rather than losing one.

ears.where: the job store does not share the application's database and outbox mode is not configured
ears.when: an application calls dbContext.EnqueueAsync
ears.shall: reject the call with an error that names outbox mode, and enqueue nothing

requirements.notes: refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-13 option 1: fail closed. The API's name promises transactional enqueue, and enqueueing outside the transaction would lose atomicity silently.

ears.shall: never create more than one job from the same outbox row, even if the relay crashes between enqueueing the job and deleting the row

ears.while: an outbox row is pending and at least one worker node is running
ears.shall: eventually enqueue its job and delete the row

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: rows are deleted by the relay once their job is enqueued (REQ-432). refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-12: provable once a running worker node is obliged to take a free relay lease (REQ-435).

ears.shall: treat a node as lost after NodeLostAfter without a heartbeat, 5 minutes by default (NodeLostAfter)

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06. Retired: moved to hosting as REQ-60 (refiner-model 2026-11-06 follow-up to dashboard F-13 and hosting F-9: NodeLostAfter is used by hosting REQ-44, dashboard REQ-341 and integrations REQ-404, and heartbeats belong to hosting, so the constant now lives in hosting; supersededBy cannot name another module's id).

ears.shall: attempt each notification delivery at most NotificationMaxAttempts times, 5 by default, with backoff from about 10 seconds to 10 minutes between attempts (NotificationMaxAttempts)

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06.

ears.shall: send at most MaxDeliveriesPerCooldown non-test deliveries per rule within its cooldown, 10 by default (MaxDeliveriesPerCooldown)

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06.

ears.when: a rule cooldown ends and deliveries for its rule were suppressed by the per-rule cap during that cooldown
ears.shall: create one digest delivery for the rule that says how many were suppressed and for which subjects

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: a flood produces up to 10 messages plus one digest, never silence.

ears.if: its channel rejects the message or cannot be reached, and NotificationMaxAttempts attempts have been made
ears.shall: mark the delivery failed, log an error that names the rule and the channel, and count it in a metric

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06. Failed deliveries are listed on the Notifications page. Same event as REQ-408.

ears.shall: default MaxRedirects for outbound calls to 0 (MaxRedirects)

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06: redirects are not followed unless the application opts in.

ears.shall: never send more than MaxDeliveriesPerCooldown non-test, non-digest deliveries for the same rule within one rule cooldown, whatever their subjects; later ones within the rule cooldown are recorded as suppressed

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06. refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-4: the rule cooldown is its own period of the rule's cooldown length, opened by INV-409.

ears.if: an HTTP job is enqueued, scheduled or defined as recurring, from code, from the launch page or from configuration, with a payload that sets an Authorization, Proxy-Authorization or Cookie header or a URL that carries user information
ears.shall: reject it with an error that points to named HttpClient registrations, and store nothing; a recurring definition from configuration is rejected when it is loaded

requirements.notes: Decided by the owner on 2026-11-06. refiner-model 2026-11-06 F-9 option 1: the check covers every creation path listed in REQ-420's notes, not only application code; before this, a launch-page or configuration job could send an Authorization header from its payload.

scenarios.title: Dead-letter alert is sent once per cooldown
scenarios.given: Rule R watches dead-lettering of job name sync-crm with a 10-minute cooldown, subject = job name; two sync-crm jobs are dead-lettered 2 minutes apart.
scenarios.then: Exactly one delivery was sent and one was recorded as suppressed.

scenarios.title: HTTP job to a host off the allowlist is refused
scenarios.given: The allowlist contains api.example.com only; an HTTP job targets http://169.254.169.254/latest.

scenarios.title: Unaccepted status fails the attempt
scenarios.given: An HTTP job accepts 200 and 204; maxAttempts = 5; the server returns 503.
scenarios.then: The job is Failed with the 503 response stored, and a retry is scheduled.

scenarios.title: Relay crash does not duplicate a job
scenarios.given: Outbox row o1 is pending; worker nodes A and B are running.

steps.note: B enqueues job o1 and crashes before deleting the row
B's lease expires and A takes it
A processes o1 again: job o1 is still stored, so nothing is created, and the row is deleted

scenarios.then: Exactly one job exists for o1, whether or not it has already finished, and o1 is no longer in the outbox.

scenarios.title: Node-lost alert fires when the last worker is down
scenarios.given: Rule R watches nodes. Worker node w1 is the only worker; web node c1 has the client and the alerts registration and no worker. w1 crashes and sends no heartbeat for NodeLostAfter.

steps.note: c1 finds w1 lost and creates a delivery

scenarios.then: One delivery for R with w1 as subject is Sent, although no worker node is running.

scenarios.title: A node without the notification lease creates no delivery
scenarios.given: Rule R watches dead-lettering. Nodes a1 and a2 both have the alerts registration; a1 holds the notification lease. A job is dead-lettered.

steps.note: a2 also tries to create a delivery for the same dead-letter

scenarios.title: A lease handover neither repeats nor loses a dead-letter alert
scenarios.given: Rule R watches dead-lettering with a subject cooldown that has already ended for every job. Nodes a1 and a2 both have the alerts registration; a1 holds the notification lease. Job e1 is dead-lettered and a1 creates its delivery. a1 then pauses past LeaseDuration, and job e2 is dead-lettered while no node holds the lease.

steps.note: a2 creates the delivery for e2

scenarios.then: There is exactly one delivery for e1 and exactly one for e2: a2 did not alert e1 again, and e2, which happened while no node held the lease, was alerted.

glossary.cooldown: Per rule, a length of time. Two periods of that length run independently: the subject cooldown (INV-400) and the rule cooldown (INV-407, REQ-414), both opened by INV-409 and held open by INV-410 while a delivery created in them is pending.
glossary.SubjectCooldown: The period, per rule and subject, in which further non-test, non-digest deliveries are suppressed (INV-400); opened by the first pending delivery for the rule and subject, closed early when that delivery fails (REQ-433).
glossary.RuleCooldown: The period, per rule, over which at most MaxDeliveriesPerCooldown deliveries are sent (INV-407) and at whose end the digest is created (REQ-414).
glossary.AlertsRegistration: The registration that lets a node evaluate notification rules and send deliveries (INV-411); independent of the client and the worker, so it can run on any node.
glossary.NotificationLease: Store lease that makes one node with the alerts registration the one that evaluates rules and sends deliveries (REQ-438).
glossary.RelayLease: Store lease that makes one worker node the outbox relay (REQ-435).
glossary.allowlist: Destination hosts outbound calls may reach; empty by default (INV-401).
glossary.MaxRedirects: Redirect limit for outbound calls; 0 by default (REQ-416).
glossary.NodeLostAfter: Time without a heartbeat after which a node is reported lost; 5 min by default (hosting REQ-60).
glossary.NotificationMaxAttempts: Attempts per notification delivery before it is Failed; 5 by default (REQ-412).
glossary.MaxDeliveriesPerCooldown: Non-test deliveries per rule within one cooldown; 10 by default (REQ-413).
